notes.title: Catizens is out in full release!
notes.content:
Hello, Pawsome!

We have some meow-tastic news to share with you - Catizens is out in full release today! Players can now experience the final chapter of Tommath, Leandra, and their fluffy comrades-in-arms' dangerous journey to save the cat kingdom.

Your resources are limited, and the final stage will take a long time to get through. Do you have what it takes?

https://youtu.be/wdg7uhMGj5Y

The full version of the game contains the following features and additions:
[list]
[*] The final level of the game: The summit of Lava Mountain. The most challenging task there is to save the Cat Kingdom. Resources are limited, and the time is ticking. Can you handle such a difficult job?
[*] The final boss: A big, scary Dragon for your cute kitties to fight!
[*] Sandbox mode: Develop your feline settlement without the campaign story restrictions. Build a cute town for your cats in various environments. Forest, Swamp, Mountain, and mixed-terrain biomes will be available in this mode.
[*] More randomized events in both game modes.
[*] New decor items to decorate cat houses. Dragons are dragons, but coziness will not create itself!
[/list]

Regards,
Catizens Team

[img]https://i.ibb.co/ZKq1vgY/2.gif[/img]

 Here's what await the catizens in the new update: 
[list]
[*] Level 6: "The Summit." This land of ash, lava, and treacherous terrain is hated by all of the cats, but they must push through for the sake of the kingdom.
[*] A mission to save the Cat Kingdom. With limited resources and no new residents, protecting the village from the destructive lava flow will not be easy, but we hope you will succeed. 
[*] The new boss is a giant dragon. He patrols the neighborhood of the volcano and raids the cat's camp. Defeating him will require coordinated teamwork and leveled-up, mighty catizens.
[*] The conclusion of an epic cat's odyssey, but will they receive a happy ending?
[/list]
The update is currently being tested and bugs are being fixed, but it will be available to all players very soon!

Regards,
Catizens Team

notes.title: Crafting better weapons for your catizens
notes.content:
Hello Pawsome!

We're continuing our series of Catizens game guides. Last time, we covered [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/957660/announcements/detail/3690182497519563154]how to cook food[/url] for catizens, as well as how to find and grow basic ingredients. Today, we're going to tell you how to equip your Knights and Rangers with more advanced weapons.

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/977dbe_86152fea560f447eabdf6679af062b45~mv2.gif[/img]
   
All of the weapons in the game are crafted by cats with the "Blacksmith" trait. From the third level of the game, you can hire a smith at the Market in exchange for a few gold coins. Before then, you'll have to make due with the weapons your cats came with.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/552f27b4e6a17ac1c6bcd5e4a19a9d0b447e9137.png[/img]

You can craft more advanced weapons for your Knights and Rangers to strengthen them against enemies: 
[list]
[*] Steel and golden swords;
[*] Recurve and golden bows;
[*] Metal shields;
[*] Knight's chest plate;
[*] Leather boots. 
[/list]
A first level blacksmith can only forge steel swords. To unlock other items, upgrade your smith cat's talents. 

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/977dbe_4c675aff1d2a4aea90b792c2af81c608~mv2.gif [/img]

You will also need special resources to craft each of these items: 
[list]
[*] [b]Metal Ore[/b] – extracted from rocks and metal ore deposits.
[*] [b]Gold[/b] – can be found in mines, obtained from rocks, or as a trophy when defeating rats.
[*] [b]Leather and sinew[/b] – obtained when hunting wolves and bears.
[*] [b]Feathers[/b] – dropped by crows when attacking your crops.
[/list]
You can also buy these items at the market, but they'll cost you.

When you have enough resources, and the right talents from the Blacksmith are available, you can start the process of making weapons in the Crafting Menu. The blacksmith will venture to the forge and begin their work. 

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/977dbe_a905502c3b9e4c1aaa0fb041c08e2a9c~mv2.gif[/img]

Tell us in the comments what other aspects of Catizens you'd like us to write about. And do not forget to join our community on [url=https://discord.gg/XVMJFp4nsP]Discord[/url], where you can quickly get answers to any questions about the game.

notes.title: How to create delicious treats in Catizens
notes.content:
Hello Pawsome! 

We're excited to tell you how to create yummy treats in Catizens. All of the kitties love eating tasty food, and some prefer certain snacks over others. The little furballs might even ask you to create something special for them.

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/977dbe_afad10667e0b4468bb9da6682de7b24f~mv2.gif[/img]

In Catizens, you can treat cats to [b]meat[/b], [b]fish[/b], [b]catnip[/b], [b]pumpkin[/b], and [b]cabbage[/b] – these are all simple foods.

However, there are also complex ones that you can craft:
[list]
[*] [b]Soup[/b] – a delicious combination of pumpkin and cabbage.
[*] [b]Bread[/b] – with a deliciously crispy crust, of course.
[*] [b]Catffine[/b] – a refreshing drink brewed from catnip.
[*] [b]Milk[/b] – what cat can't resist a saucer of milk?
[*] [b]Cheese[/b] – it's also a treat for rats, which means it can be used to negotiate a truce.
[/list]

[h2]How to get simple tasty treats[/h2]

You can obtain [b]meat[/b] by slaying wild boars and other predators in the area.

Catizens with the Fisher trait can catch [b]fish[/b] in a nearby river. Just tell them where the fishing spot is and they'll cast their lines.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/900b895057fbe30f9bd147cd33121760ded7dbc9.png[/img] 

[b]Catnip[/b] grows around the settlements. You can also grow it in the fields if you fulfill a request from a cat with the Catnip Lover trait. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/8deb7a64839cb0698bbc8cbad5152512f06080c2.png[/img]

[b]Cabbage[/b] and [b]pumpkins[/b] are grown and harvested by farmer cats and do not require any special attention from you. The only thing you'll need to do is fend off annoying flocks of crows who want to eat your delicious crops, but building a scarecrow will keep them away.

[h2]How to prepare these complex delicacies[/h2]

It will take a lot of effort to create [b]milk[/b], [b]bread[/b], [b]cheese[/b], [b]soup[/b], or [b]Cattfin[/b]. You have to spend time developing your farmers and honing their talents.

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/977dbe_c88ea4022d1445af831b1b1d2efa5431~mv2.gif[/img]

[h3]Milk[/h3]

Build a Stable and buy a few cows, who will start producing [b]milk[/b] . You'll be able to build the Stables after unlocking the appropriate farmer cat talent.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/2216003f161ecf0e16228cac44617ed2d8bb588b.png[/img]

Cows produce milk every 25 in-game hours. The farmer cat will milk the cow and take the milk to the warehouse – you do not need to take any additional steps to get it.

[h3]Soup and Cheese[/h3]

To make [b]soup [/b]or [b]cheese[/b], you need a cat with the “Basic Cooking” talent. You may build an Outdoor Kitchen as soon as a kitty with that talent appears in your settlement. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/ec5a42ab77caf24ace4ab711b400990ef2df0ac6.png[/img]

The [b]soup[/b] is made from cabbage and pumpkin, and cheese is made from milk. You already know how to obtain these resources, so it'll be easy to satisfy the needs of your catizens.

[h3]Bread[/h3]

Catizens love [b]bread[/b], but you'll need flour, wheat, and a windmill to make it. The first step is to assign the "Wheat" and "Windmill" traits to a farmer kitty, then the Windmill will be available in the build menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/e7352bba7dfa090c4da68f3398a8742d068fa5a6.png[/img]
 
The farmers will plant, water, and then harvest the wheat as sheaves. The other catizens will then collect the sheaves and take them to the storehouse. Once there is wheat in the store, the flour-making process will automatically start.

To bake bread, you need to unlock a farmer's "Bread" talent. After that, the cats can use the stove at the Outdoor Kitchen.

[h3]Catffine[/h3]

And, finally, the last delicious thing that lifts the spirits of all kitties: [b]catffine[/b]. To create it, you need to unlock the farmer's "Tavern" talent and then build a tavern.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/3b5e376c4e8631a9d3e130daf2a02e5b95c96d9f.png[/img]

[h2]Crafting Menu[/h2]

You'll need the Crafting Menu to begin the process of making soup, bread, cheese and catffine. Open the menu and select the desired number of dishes. After that, the cat farmer will go to the Outdoor Kitchen, or the Tavern, to prepare the goodies. 

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/977dbe_43ae326c9a4c4a2987a3795a835caf56~mv2.gif [/img]

We hope you're excited about creating treats for the kitties of the cat kingdom.

Tell us in the comments what other aspects of Catizens you'd like us to write about. And do not forget to join our community on [url=https://discord.gg/XVMJFp4nsP]Discord[/url], where you can quickly get answers to any questions about the game.

notes.title: New patch released and more content on the way!
notes.content:
Hello, pawsome! 

We received so much fantastic feedback about Catizens that we needed to get a giant new table for all of the notes! The Catizens community is fantastic and responsive when it comes to helping us with the game.

[img]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/977dbe_59853cb96a95481fb4546d0744abee94~mv2.gif[/img]

Rest assured, we've gone through all of the comments, suggestions, and bugs. This update contains bug fixes and improvements to the base game, as well as some new content.

[h3][b]Important: You will need to create a new save file to enjoy some of the bug fixes as the existing saves for the sandbox mode remain broken. Sorry about that![/b][/h3]

What's new:
[list]
[*] Moved camera rotation control to the left mouse button in order to avoid conflicts when players issued instructions to catizens via the same button. This sometimes led to player issued commands being canceled when the player unintentionally rotated the camera.
[*] Creating the multi-selection box now allocated to shift + left click to drag.
[*] Fog of war will no longer return to full strength at night.
[*] Fog of war is a bit lighter and easier to see through for explored areas.
[*] Goldmines in all sandbox modes are now accessible.
[*] You can now change the name of all new catizens. Select the character, move the mouse over their name on the bottom left, and an edit pencil will pop up.
[*] Removed green text in tooltips – they are normal text colors now.
[*] Implemented ranger talent: Marksmanship and Rain of Arrows
[*] A large rat boss will appear in the sandbox mode.
[*] Added an Architect talent to move a building to a new location without having to rebuild. Select an architect (that has learned the ability), click on the ability, and select a building to move (left or right click on a building). That will open the build menu to let you place it in a new location. This ability has a 48-hour cooldown. Expectedly, this will disrupt the lives of anyone currently in and around the building.
[/list]
[b]Even more content in the works![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/557aeeb15da3278fcdd97691056b6e4ba6ff4e62.png[/img]

You can also buy rare items from the market, like flea collars, which are essential for the comfortable life of your catizens. And if you're in desperate need of a cat with paws in the right place, you can hire a farmer, an architect, a knight or even a ranger.

notes.title: From your average colony simulator to cat empire
notes.content:
Hello, pawsome!

Like many video games, Catizens has evolved since its original conception. When the game was first conceived, there were no cats at all! How truly paw-ful! The game started out as a colony simulator with people, with the idea of kitty cats coming in later. 

The very first concepts of catizens captured the hearts of everyone on the team. From that point forward, there was no turning back. How was it even possible to compete with such adorable-looking warriors?

But how did we turn human models into cats? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/4ab70205b73529b7233fcfb4118681f04ab0b3fd.png[/img]

Creating anthropomorphic cats is not as easy as it sounds. They have to move like humans, do fully human-like actions, like chopping trees or planting cabbage, all the while maintaining a cat-like appearance and habits. 

Fur was an additional problem. Creating a fur coat composed of individual hairs is a long and expensive process. Also, one cannot make cats just chubby and pass it off as fluffy; the textures would run through each other. The process isn't over, and we're still working hard to create convincing fur for each catizen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/2d01d55898303d86793d2e5b9d5d969e8cdfc6b0.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/3b15b64375920b580da6441928af110ff47d6cd1.png[/img]

Okay, we've got the body sorted out, but what about the head? How do we create cute cartoon-looking heads while avoiding the dreaded uncanny valley effect? As you can see, there were many options we had to go through to achieve the right balance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/d6120fe7b4f437234180ff3f2049f38d6f975b09.png[/img]

Another difficulty was clothing. Was it necessary? How many items of clothing would cats wear? In the end, we decided that freedom-loving cats do not favor putting on too many "human" clothes. That is why, of all the elements of clothing, only headgear and tools were left. Cats of different professions wear different hats, so you can more easily identify them. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/f9c093211ea1daedb718837304009c1376088951.png[/img]

Regular catizens differ from each other by their fur color, different eye colors and the shape of their ears. And typical cat names only add to the resemblance to real pets. Can't get a real cat at home? Then build your cat empire with Catizens!

Respectfully,
Catizens Team

notes.title: The forest beasts of Catizens
notes.content:
Hello pawsome!

The world of Catizens is certainly cozy, but it is also not without danger! The woods are filled with beasts that will attack any kitty on sight. We've [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/957660/announcements/detail/4509778749595957119] previously talked [/url] about the evil rats in Catizens, but today we want to show you some of the other enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/f8d68da9eae717c4746248c9e1cdef615487a370.png[/img]

The wild boars are the most basic enemy in the game. They live in the woods and tend to travel in groups of two or three. Thankfully, they're easy to defeat and will drop a lot of delicious meat for the catizens. Unless you are dealing with the boss boar, of course. Stay away from him.

Then we have the wolves, ferocious predators that can do more damage than boars. Your catizens will be safe during the day as wolves hunt at night. To put an end to the wolves, you will need to defeat the wolf pack leader who lives in a den, but it won't be easy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/cb64e0cbd2de1d293a1b505fe2b77468312b9bf6.png[/img]

And then we have the bears. They live in caves and will roam around on their own. The bears have an excellent sense of smell and are always on the hunt for food, which includes raiding your storage sheds. But if you let the bears eat their fill of your supplies, they will wander off and leave your settlement alone. Be careful if you want to attack one of them – bears have thick skins and sharp claws! 

Don't let catizens go into the dark forest unprotected! Leandra and her knights are always ready to help and guard the settlement, as well as its inhabitants. 

Respectfully,
Catizens Team

notes.title: Building a better tomorrow for happy kitties
notes.content:
Hello, pawsome!

Your catizens are finicky creatures of comfort. It's not enough to have a few houses erected and call it a day, you will need to improve the various buildings in your settlement to keep everyone happy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/1a6e9342d3a126affc34ca7aa9dfe01c3cfa4134.png[/img]

Luckily, you can upgrade most of the structures in the game. You might want to put a wool-stuffed mattress in a house so the cat has an extra-comfortable nap, but that will take a few extra steps and resources. You will need to train a shepherd, then build a barn and raise a few sheep after. After that, it's finally time to shear the sheep for their fluffy wool!

Another example of upgraded buildings is the market. The base version will only allow you to trade goods with sales-cats, but once it is upgraded, you can employ professionals to bolster your ranks, farmers, and more.

Remember, the standard of living has a direct influence on the mood of your catizens. A settlement with happy kitties has a better chance of making the journey to Lava Meowntain!

Respectfully,
Catizens Team

notes.title: Go Rangers!
notes.content:
Hello, pawsome!

Have you noticed kitties wearing green caps and carrying bows in some of the Catizens screenshots and videos? These furry friends are so meow-sterious that they haven't even shown up in the game yet! Today, we'd like to introduce you to the rangers. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/4b2ce1f1e37514b73c24c30568999699e1f9dd67.jpg[/img]

The rangers are warriors just like the knights, but instead of rushing into battle, they prefer to attack from a distance. Pairing a knight and ranger together is the purr-fect combination to protect your settlement.

You can place several rangers around your town to pick off any rats that dare to attack your catizens. A hail of arrows might not stop the vermin, but they'll give the knights the upper paw in melee combat.

But please don't send the rangers alone into any dangerous situations. While they are masters of the bow, they wear very weak armor, which makes them susceptible to attacks.

Any catizen can train to be a ranger, but some of them will be better suited to the job than others. For example, a kitty with the "hunter" trait will allow the ranger to stealthily track an enemy. Of course, it's up to you to decide which feline can be a ranger, and we can't wait to see the different combinations that players come up with!


Respectfully,
Catizens Team

notes.title: Be the purr-fect leader!
notes.content:
Hello, pawsome!

To build a successful settlement for your catizens, you'll need more than just new buildings and resources. According to the Purrs-low hierarchy of needs, after satisfying their cravings for delicious food, a safe home and good friends, your kitties will develop personal desires. If the catizens aren't nurtured, they will become dissatisfied with the colony and leave.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/0de7f6d2b5843d051f892a187052fdd65e590352.jpg[/img]

You will need to pay attention to the distinctive traits of each cat. For example, some of them adore other animals and want to live near a barn with sheep and cows. By fulfilling this small request, it will strengthen the cat's faith in your town and they will be happier. 

Another cat may prefer to eat raw food and sleep on the ground -- they feel the call of their ancient ancestors. Make sure your settlement is stocked up on raw meat and perfect places for cat naps.

Cats with comfortable living conditions that fit their needs will happily work for the good of the settlement! But if you ignore their requests, they will leave and never return.

Be the purr-fect feline leader! You can do it! 

Respectfully,
Catizens Team

notes.title: Meet the rat thieves!
notes.content:
Hello pawsome!

You've already encountered terrible goblins while playing the Catizens demo, right? The creepy creatures that attack in groups, steal food and even catizens! What pawful monsters!

We're here to tell you that the goblins were just prototypes! We wanted the creatures in Catizens to be ruthless and mean to cats, but we just couldn't decide which creatures to use. Should we use people? No, they are too big and dumb for the world of Catizens. What about snakes? Maybe, but they don't have any hands...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/f41b27ddfa939980c19b4d42c92adb824456996f.jpg[/img]

...and then it came to us: rats! They can be strong, aggressive, and insidious. Rats are a fearsome foe for cats looking to save their world. After all, not every Catizen is a warrior that can take on an entire band of menacing rats.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/2af3608034e39557a7892530d99af6d3d0119d24.png[/img]

The rats in Catizens hunger for food and a world without pesky cats. Not to mention that the rats know how to defend themselves, which means you're going to need to train a lot of kitty cat knights to protect your cosy town! 

Until next time,
Catizens Team

notes.title: A full belly makes a happy kitty
notes.content:
Hello pawsome!

The forest is dark and full of danger, but it's not the enemies lurking in the shadows you should worry about. The number one hazard for any settlement is lack of food. Today, we will tell you all about nourishment in the world of Catizens, as well as ways to keep your cats well fed. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/6cf770f2cb077072f2ef11262ec00240dd84012a.png[/img]

At the very beginning, hunting and fishing will be your main sources of food. It is important to use the right catizens even for these basic activities. Meat is obtained from wild boars that can be dangerous to an unarmed kitty, so make sure you have a Knight roaming the forest and looking to bring home some bacon. To catch fish one needs to have a cat with the fishing trait. Not every catizen can bear the stress of catching food that actively tries to swim away! 

After you make progress on your settlement’s infrastructure, you will be able to hire a farmer cat that can grow vegetables. Plant-based nutrition plays an important role in the diets of most predators, let alone adorable cats :) Pumpkins and cabbages will help your catizens maintain nutritional balance and avoid being hungry if there’s a shortage of other types of food.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/8e8306fb00307f53365c4edba4eabe66142c8c5e.png[/img]

Soon enough, your farmers will level up and the settlement will have access to more advanced building types. A shepherd can breed cows and sheep in order to provide your settlement with milk and wool. Mmm, milk ^ _ ^

A chef knows how to bake bread and make soup. So regardless of whether you have a bunch of tree cats running amok or a group of petulant house cats chilling in the bath house, you can always provide your catizens with food to satisfy a variety of tastes and needs.  

Respectfully,
Catizens Team

notes.title: Cozy cats and cozy beds
notes.content:
Hello pawsome!

If you observe cats in the real world, you’ll notice that they are not opposed to the idea of making their homes more comfy. We’ve improved upon this idea in Catizens, where your furry minions can build a whole town :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/89adfb3adf31ab4bfce1282d3e5724a055d68fa2.png[/img]

Cats can sleep up to 16 hours a day, which is why we have put a lot of focus on their houses. Each one has a little bed or two so that your catizens can be cozy and safe while resting.

When choosing housing for each cat, you will have to take into account their needs: quiet cats prefer to settle in single houses away from noisy neighbors. The friendly and the sociable, on the contrary, are ready to share life with other cats so that there is always someone to play or purr with. Tree lovers need a bed on the second floor – far away from the ground. There are a few Catizens who also prefer a simple tent to nap in. The level of satisfaction of your furry inhabitants and their loyalty to the city and fellow settlers will depend on the comforts you can provide them with.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/e8a09e0a9c6bf94e2e11cd310fdd7349ac5fddb8.png[/img]

This is where house decorations come into play, but they require you to train your catizens in a range of professions, and to extract a lot of resources from the surrounding lands.

Our team is currently busy with adding more decorations and coming up with additional ways to customize houses in the game. By the time Catizens launches, you should have everything you need to make the purrfect place for your cats!

Respectfully,
Catizens Team

notes.title: Meet Leandra & Tommath
notes.content:
Hello, pawsome!

Today, we're going to talk about the two pointy-eared stars of Catizens: Tommath and Leandra! It is your job to guide them to the Lava Meowntain, help them establish relationships with other cats and build a safe haven for everybody.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/a55afcb10a8da88be054a383118b40e4af91b338.png[/img]

Tommath is an architect by trade, and he loves it! He will be the first cat to lay the foundation of your settlement. His hardworking paws will build cottages, farms, kitchens and markets. His concern is anything that will make the lives of catizens more comfortable.

Leandra is a brave warrior that is always ready to defend your settlement from enemy attacks. Until she trains more knights, Leandra is the only thing standing between the cozy town and the harsh wilds of the world. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/af9d1f10678261eeadb9c07659947c303770dda4.png[/img]

At the beginning of the game, you will have the opportunity to customize the two protagonists. You can change their colour, facial expressions and many other characteristics and traits. You can even make them look and act like your own cats!

These two will lead a brave band of followers to the top of the Lava Meowntain, where it's up to them to stop the destruction of the Cat Kingdom. Under your watchful eye, of course!

Respectfully,
Catizens Team

notes.title: Cat professions and vital resources
notes.content:
Hello pawsome!

In the real-world, cats are pretty content with having a place to sleep, food to eat and keyboards to lie on. In the world of Catizens, your furry minions can sometimes be more demanding, but they do give back. 

Even the regular cats, the ones without a profession, are still willing to work for the Cat Kingdom! In fact, they will chop down trees, mine stone and gold, as well as carry harvests back to the warehouse. With their help, you'll have the basic materials needed to construct most of the buildings you'll need to grow your settlement. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/194870ff61023804facc8f4a759d90744789ffa2.jpg[/img]

The beasts in a nearby forest can be fairly aggressive, so even finding food is dangerous. If you want your catizens well-fed, you're going to either need a well-armed knight to fight the wildlife off or a cat with a river cat to fish the waters.

All of your hard work will pay off as you'll later unlock farms, cookhouses and the chef profession to feed your Catizens the healthiest, most delicious meals and to keep them fighting-fit!

As your settlement grows, you're gonna have a surplus of certain resources, but a decline of others. This is where trading plays into Catizens. Merchants will visit your settlement and bring with them all manner of goods, most of which you'll need. And after some reasonable (or unreasonable) trades, they'll be on their way.

Eventually, you’ll be able to build large multi-story houses. These are a favorite for tree cats to live in, as they love to sleep high above the ground. You’ll also be able to build saunas and corrals, and can top it all off with decorative buildings, fulfilling the needs of every cat. It may not be easy, but it’ll definitely be fun!

Until next time,
Catizens Team

notes.title: Living The Cat Life
notes.content:
Hello pawsome!

A feast for the eyes​ is a well-known idiom that shows just how impawrtant visuals are in creating an experience one can enjoy and believe in. Naturally, we wanted to make sure the world of Catizens reflects the cat theme in as many ways as possible, with each major detail fitting neatly into the game’s overall style and atmosphere. Otherwise, there wouldn’t be much of a cat fantasy world, would it?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/e54e4e2bd8550224059c1d72dcbaf342bc0485cb.jpg[/img]

The most obvious way of presenting the game’s theme, besides catizens themselves, is via the game’s environment and the buildings and objects your cats interact with. We’ve included a feline motif throughout the settlement the catizens inhabit, with the intention of creating a sense that this place is populated by individuals with paws and whiskers, not humans.

Soft beds and sturdy walls go hand in hand with wooden scratching poles. After all, it’s important to keep your tools of the trade in tip-top shape!

Though the catizens walk on two paws and are perhaps a tad more anthropomorphic than a typical house cat, they have preserved some of their ancestors’ quirks and habits. Stretching out on a soft pillow, playing with a ball of yarn, smuggling a bushel of catnip — these aren’t just gameplay elements, they help make the world more believable and purr-suasive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/8b056f1eceb0650abea451ea52aeb26fcba8d72d.png[/img]

One could endlessly speculate on what the world would look like if felines had become the dominant species in place of apes. Yet, our vision of the game is thoroughly human — cute and cozy, permeated with adoration for the furry overlords that pretend to be our pets. 

Until next time,
Catizens Team

notes.title: Kitties & Knights - Catizens Unite
notes.content:
Hello pawsome!

Starting today, we will provide you with important news on the development of Catizens and the creation of our feline world. Let’s begin!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/75ecb52eb664d6bb94c98690b7ab5c25e798a1ee.jpg[/img]

Today, we'll tell you about the range of diversity in the world of Catizens. The inhabitants aren't anonymous whiskered drones that simply complete tasks, they have a purr-sonality to match and a life of their own. 

Each cat can have up to three traits that form the basis of its personality, and we did our best to make sure none of the traits are definitively positive or negative. 

For example, brave cats are excellent fighters who will rush headlong into battle – they’re your furry defense against any troubles, be it wild animals or more dangerous, monstrous creatures. But be careful, for valorous knights will even go so far as to sacrifice their lives to protect their friends. Be sure to keep an eye on them, or they may perish while protecting the town!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38790098/858c88004f4f2843cb28945693e9e17f41e4bb03.jpg[/img]

Many traits are necessary to unlock objectives and fulfill tasks. Cowardly cats will avoid any kind of battle and hide until it's safe for them. However, with a cowardly catizen, you'll gain access to the training dummy. Who, after all, better understands the importance of self-defense than a coward? Their cat-titude is: “If I'm not ready to protect the town, someone else will have to be!"

Nocturnal cats prefer to sleep during the day – once the sun sets, their energy is boundless. If you need work done after dark, or if you’d just like to observe some feline nightlife, nocturnal cats are the cats for you. And they’ll even provide you access to lamps to decorate the town.

Pets of all kin and kind will be under your control — gregarious and shy, lazy and eager, pacifists and curmudgeons. There are dozens of traits to be explored and endless paw-sibilities for different catizens! With the right approach, cats can build a prosperous society together ...with your help, of course.

This message is cat approved! 

Until next time,
Catizens Team
